On a dependable stretch, rules for the ramp team
This section explains the steps for the whole desk
Companion Animal Travel Desk Service Rules

This section keeps animal travel handling steady, clear, and courteous from check-in through handoff. Staff confirm the booking details, review the crate condition, and record every service change in the desk ledger before the case moves on. If a traveler reports a problem with a crate, the coordinator listens, logs the facts, and keeps the discussion calm and direct. <<FACT F118>> The desk does not guess at outcomes, and no promise goes out until the review is complete.

When a trip breaks down because a connection is missed, staff note what happened, add the report to the ledger, and route the case through the normal review path. <<FACT F110>> Travelers should get plain guidance, not loose talk, and the team should keep the next step simple and visible. If the animal needs special care, the coordinator checks the file, shares the handling note with the ramp team, and makes sure the transfer stays smooth. Ruby or any other pet gets the same careful treatment, no shortcuts and no side chatter.

Any escalation should move up one level at a time, with the senior coordinator taking the lead only after the first review is done. Keep messages short, factual, and respectful, and leave a clean record in the ledger for the next shift. For any open issue, contact the senior coordinator at Aurelia Skyways or the duty supervisor on the floor.
